connect.connectionsDesc: Each connection binds a workspace, config file, channel, and agent.
connect.runtimeDesc: The connection below defines which channel and agent Bridge will use.
connect.configHint: Channel and agent settings live in local SQLite; agentlink.toml is written when Bridge starts or you save config.
connect.devPathHint: Dev mode uses target/release and examples paths in the repo.
connect.prodPathHint: Release builds use the bundled agentlink binary; writable config is stored under Application Support.
connect.startBlockedScanBind: Complete scan bind for {channel} on the Channel tab first
connect.startBlockedChannel: Complete {channel} configuration on the Channel tab first
connect.startBlockedAgent: Configure and check the Agent on the Agent tab first

channel.listDesc: Pick a chat platform. Credentials are stored locally and written to TOML when Bridge starts.
channel.boundHint: This channel is already bound. Tap “Scan again” above to switch account or refresh token.
channel.fillBeforeScan: Fill required fields below, then tap Scan to bind.
channel.manualHintScan: You can switch to scan binding, or save manual credentials and start Bridge from Connect.
channel.manualHintGuided: Complete setup on the platform console first, then use the guide here (not an auto-auth QR).
channel.manualHintDefault: Enter credentials below, save, then start Bridge from Connect.

test.title: Targets & test send
test.desc: A target is a user, group, or webhook. Only one agent may use a target at a time.
test.noTargets: No targets yet. Refresh after someone messages the bot.
test.targetLocked: This target is used by {connection} / {agent}. Only one agent per target at a time.
test.advancedRoutingHint: Internal routing fields; usually filled by “Refresh targets”.
test.step2: Send a message to the bot on the real channel
test.directSendSupported: {channel} supports direct test send from the client.
test.directSendUnsupported: {channel} does not support direct test send. Message the bot first or use the HTTP test channel.
test.defaultContent: Please help me verify this test message
test.receiveIdPlaceholder: Leave empty to discover from inbound messages

agent.listDesc: Agent settings are stored locally and written to TOML when Bridge starts.
agent.linkHint: This agent pairs with the selected channel; inbound messages route here when Bridge runs.
agent.linkHintNamed: {agent} will handle messages from {channel} when Bridge runs.

about.positionDesc: AgentLink connects Feishu, DingTalk, WeChat, Telegram, and more to Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor Agent, and other coding agents.
about.step1: On Connect, confirm executable, config, and workspace.
about.step2: On Channel, pick a platform and bind via scan or credentials.
about.step3: Start Bridge, then send a message to the bot on the real channel.
about.step4: Refresh targets and pick a user, group, or webhook.
about.step5: On Agent, choose Codex or another agent and verify the command.
about.step6: Start Bridge from Connect; replies flow back to the channel.
about.trayDesc: Closing the window hides to tray. Quit from the tray menu to stop Bridge and exit.
about.designDesc: One target binds to one agent at a time. Advanced routing fields exist for power users; daily use only needs channel, target, and agent.

log.title: Log
log.ready: Client ready. Create connections and pick channel and agent.
log.devPathsReset: Reset AgentLink executable to dev default (target/release/agentlink).

qr.weixinHelp: After scan, token and account_id are saved. Send a WeChat message to cache context_token.
qr.qqHelp: Scan on the QQ gateway (e.g. NapCat), then set ws_url here.
qr.dingtalkHelp: No keys needed upfront. Scan with DingTalk, tap create robot on the page; Client ID and Client Secret are saved automatically. Robot Code is optional.
qr.wecomHelp: No keys needed upfront. Scan with WeCom and confirm creating the smart bot; Bot ID and Secret are saved for WebSocket mode.
qr.genericHelp: Use the link below to finish setup on the platform console.
